transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Samira Khan, Diego Ramos, Priya Nair (Redwood) - Lena Patel, Marco Chen, Sara Lewis, Tom Rivera (AstraNova)

Summary: quick intro; AstraNova currently on OpenAI with ~2M tokens/month, exploring Dedicated for cost and predictable latency; worried about model parity, vLLM/TGI stack differences, and security.

00:00:02 Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samira from Redwood, i'll kick off. can folks introduce themselves quickly?
00:00:12 Lena: lena, cto at astranova, thanks for doing this.
00:00:15 Marco: marco, ml eng manager, i run the inference pipelines.
00:00:18 Sara: sara, security lead. mostly here for compliance questions.
00:00:22 Tom: tom, infra, i'll help with networking questions.
00:00:25 Diego: diego, solutions eng on infra/runtime side. we'll dig into perf.
00:00:30 Samira: high level, we want to understand your current usage, primary goals for migration, and blockers. feel free to interrupt at any point.
00:00:40 Lena: quick context — we've been on openai for ~18 months. main product uses chat completions for customer support automation and a reranker for search. monthly spend ~2k-ish, wait, sorry 2M tokens, about $10k. latency's variable and sometimes spikes which impacts SLAs. we're evaluating whether Redwood Dedicated gives predictable latency and lower unit costs.
00:01:05 Marco: also model parity is big — our prompts are tuned to gpt-4o-ish behavior. we need the responses to match our evals, or we need a re-eval plan.
00:01:18 Sara: for us, SOC2, audit logs, and KMS + customer-managed keys are must-haves. SSO integration is required.
00:01:26 Diego: thanks. quick question on current infra — are you using any self-hosted inference libs like vLLM or TGI in prod?
00:01:32 Marco: no, we don't run vLLM ourselves. we experimented with TGI for local testing but it's not production. openai is our production endpoint.
00:01:40 Priya: got it. that shapes options. Redwood Dedicated can run curated open models and also provide managed routing to variants. compatibility with openai calls is usually straightforward via our API or an OpenAI-compat shim — has anyone tried simulating traffic?
00:01:56 Tom: not yet. our infra team needs clear network requirements and egress rules for private deployment or VPC peering.
00:02:02 Diego: noted. on the model side, you'd be looking at two things: run-time behavior (latency, kv-cache handling) and model output parity (tokenization, sampling). we typically run eval parity tests with the customer's prompt set to compare.
00:02:20 Marco: can you support the same sampling params, temperature, top_p, etc? that's important to reproduce outputs.
00:02:25 Diego: yes, we support the same parameters. minor differences can occur if model weights differ; if you're using an OpenAI proprietary model we map to the closest open variant or we can host licensed versions if available.
00:02:39 Lena: what about vLLM/TGI differences? we ran into some mismatch when switching between runtime stacks in staging.
00:02:45 Diego: good point — vLLM/TGI have different kernel behaviors and sometimes different tokenization or batching defaults. on Redwood Dedicated, our runtime optimizes kernels and respects your tokenization and sampling settings. for POC we include a vLLM/TGI comparison in the benchmark to highlight any deltas.
00:02:59 Samira: can you walk through typical migration flow? like pilot > bench > rollout.
00:03:05 Priya: typical is 1) sizing and capacity plan, 2) benchmarking with your prompt set and traffic profile, 3) pilot on dedicated pool with canary routing, 4) production cutover with rollback policies. we support canary/A-B and autoscale policies.
00:03:20 Marco: about benchmarks — we need to know latency p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens. what workload size can you simulate?
00:03:29 Diego: for the POC we can simulate your real traffic shape. our standard bench runs 5k-20k requests/day for two weeks to capture variance. we'll return p50/p90/p95 latencies, throughput, and cost modeling.
00:03:40 Sara: encryption — do you support CMEK?
00:03:43 Priya: yes, customer-managed keys supported in Redwood Private and in Dedicated with KMS integrations. we'll share the integration guide. audit logs and retention options are configurable.
00:03:52 Tom: network — VPC peering vs private deployment? what's recommended for a company with strict egress rules?
00:03:58 Diego: for strict egress we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). Dedicated can be deployed in a customer VPC depending on the package; otherwise we have peering options and private endpoints. we'll send the network checklist.
00:04:10 Lena: licensing — if we need a specific model family that's not open, can you host it?
00:04:16 Priya: we can support licensed models on Dedicated or Private when licensing allows; otherwise we map to a proximate open model and run evals to ensure parity. sometimes customers license a model directly and bring weights.
00:04:26 Marco: about accuracy/regression — how do you track quality differences?
00:04:29 Diego: we run automated evals on your gold prompts and produce regression alerts. Redwood Optimize has features for quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. for the POC we'll run the exact eval suite you provide and produce a scoring report.
00:04:42 Marco: great. what about burst capacity? our support chats have spiky traffic.
00:04:46 Priya: Dedicated supports burst configs and autoscaling policies; we can reserve baseline GPUs and allow burst to cloud capacity. SLA options differ by contract.
00:04:55 Sara: compliance — do you provide penetration test results and third-party audits?
00:04:58 Samira: yes, SOC 2, plus we have pen test summaries and can provide third-party audit reports under NDA.
00:05:04 Tom: curious about the OpenAI-compat shim — is there a drop-in or do we have to rework code?
00:05:09 Diego: we offer an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that maps common endpoints; most customers switch with minimal code changes. we also provide SDK examples and a migration checklist.
00:05:20 Marco: sample prompts — we'll share our top 200 prompts and the reranker dataset. is that enough for parity testing?
00:05:25 Priya: yes, that plus traffic shape and token length distribution is ideal.
00:05:30 Lena: timeline — ideally we want a pilot within 3 weeks; is that realistic?
00:05:34 Samira: yes, with quick exchange of prompts and access we can do a 2-week benchmark and pilot in that window.
00:05:40 Diego: i'll coordinate the benchmark plan and test harness; we'll need an API key to simulate calls or we can mirror logs.
00:05:47 Marco: one more infra question: KV cache handling — our app relies on long-context caching across sessions. any gotchas?
00:05:54 Diego: our runtime exposes KV cache controls and supports long-context sessions; when migrating, we'll measure throughput changes due to KV cache behavior. some runtime differences can affect warm vs cold latencies but we'll surface that in the bench.
00:06:08 Sara: data retention — can you set retention windows and disable logs for specific endpoints?
00:06:11 Priya: yes, we have configurable retention and redaction rules; we can exclude certain endpoints from logs for compliance.
00:06:20 Samira: okay to recap next steps?
00:06:23 Samira: action items: Samira will share pricing; Diego will draft benchmark; Marco will send prompts + traffic profile; Sara will send compliance checklist; all due early next week.
00:06:36 Lena: sounds good, thanks.
00:06:38 Tom: thanks everyone.
00:06:40 Diego: we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
00:06:44 Samira: end of meeting, thanks.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words and slight speaker mislabels in export. There were minor overlaps when multiple participants chimed in. Some proper nouns (vLLM/TGI) were spelled correctly but occasionally mis-heard in the raw transcript.

References mentioned: Dedicated pricing sheet (link shared later), SOC2 + ISO compliance pack (link), network checklist (link), benchmark template (link).

End of transcript.
